title: Palpitations Differential Diagnosis
description: Differential diagnosis for palpitations in adults, covering cardiac arrhythmic, structural cardiac, psychosomatic, systemic, and drug/substance-related etiologies.
source_description: Raviele A, Giada F, Bergfeldt L, Blanc JJ, Blomstrom-Lundqvist C, Mont L, Morgan JM, Raatikainen MJP, Steinbeck G, Viskin S, et al. Management of patients with palpitations: a position paper from the European Heart Rhythm Association. Europace 2011;13(7):920-934.

diagnoses.name: Ventricular Tachycardia
key_features: Rapid regular palpitations with abrupt onset
Associated presyncope or syncope
History of structural heart disease or prior MI
Wide-complex tachycardia on ECG
red_flags: Family history of sudden cardiac death

diagnoses.name: Atrial Fibrillation / Atrial Flutter
key_features: Irregularly irregular palpitations (AF) or regular rapid palpitations (flutter)
May be paroxysmal with sudden onset and offset
Associated dyspnea, fatigue, or exercise intolerance
Irregular pulse on examination
red_flags: Rapid ventricular rate with hemodynamic compromise
recommended_tests: Ambulatory ECG monitoring (Holter or event monitor)

diagnoses.name: Supraventricular Tachycardia (SVT)
key_features: Regular rapid palpitations with abrupt onset and offset
Sensation of fluttering or racing in the chest or neck
Polyuria after episode (ANP release)
Responsive to vagal maneuvers
red_flags: Pre-excitation on resting ECG (delta wave suggesting WPW)

diagnoses.name: Premature Atrial and Ventricular Complexes
key_features: Sensation of skipped beats or extra beats
Isolated thumping followed by a pause
Often intermittent and position-dependent
May worsen with caffeine, stress, or fatigue
red_flags: Very frequent PVCs (>10% burden) may cause cardiomyopathy

diagnoses.name: Sinus Tachycardia
key_features: Gradual onset and offset of rapid heartbeat
Heart rate 100-150 bpm with normal P waves on ECG
Often associated with identifiable trigger (exercise, fever, anxiety)
Appropriate physiological response to stress or illness
red_flags: Persistent unexplained sinus tachycardia (consider PE, sepsis, hemorrhage)
Inappropriate sinus tachycardia without identifiable cause

diagnoses.name: Bradyarrhythmias (Sick Sinus Syndrome / AV Block)
key_features: Palpitations from compensatory pauses or escape beats
Associated presyncope, dizziness, or fatigue
Alternating bradycardia and tachycardia (tachy-brady syndrome)
Slow pulse on examination
recommended_tests: Ambulatory ECG monitoring (extended if infrequent symptoms)
Electrophysiological study if high-grade block suspected

diagnoses.name: Anxiety and Panic Disorder
key_features: Palpitations with gradual onset after emotional stress
Associated hyperventilation, paresthesias, and sense of doom
Normal cardiac rhythm during symptoms
Recurrent episodes often in specific settings
recommended_tests: Ambulatory ECG monitoring during symptomatic episode

diagnoses.name: Hyperthyroidism
key_features: Palpitations with sinus tachycardia or atrial fibrillation
Heat intolerance, weight loss, tremor
Diffuse or nodular goiter on examination
Warm moist skin, lid lag
red_flags: Thyroid storm (fever, tachycardia, altered mental status)
New-onset atrial fibrillation secondary to thyrotoxicosis

diagnoses.name: Structural Heart Disease (Valvular / Cardiomyopathy)
key_features: Palpitations associated with exertional dyspnea
Mitral valve prolapse click and murmur
Signs of heart failure (elevated JVP, peripheral edema)
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with dynamic outflow obstruction
red_flags: Family history of sudden cardiac death (HCM, ARVC)

diagnoses.name: Drug and Substance-Induced Palpitations
key_features: Temporal relationship with substance use
Caffeine, alcohol, nicotine, or stimulant use
Sympathomimetic medications (bronchodilators, decongestants)
Beta-blocker withdrawal
recommended_tests: Toxicology screen if substance abuse suspected

also_consider.name: Pheochromocytoma / Paraganglioma
also_consider.rationale: Episodic palpitations with hypertension, headache, and diaphoresis (classic triad); check plasma metanephrines

also_consider.name: Brugada Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: Inherited channelopathy with characteristic coved ST elevation in V1-V3; risk of VF and sudden death in young adults

also_consider.name: Long QT Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: Congenital or acquired QT prolongation predisposing to torsades de pointes; check QTc on baseline ECG and medication review

also_consider.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: Accessory pathway causing pre-excitation (delta wave on ECG); risk of rapid AF with hemodynamic collapse

also_consider.name: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS)
also_consider.rationale: Heart rate increase of 30+ bpm on standing with palpitations, lightheadedness; more common in young women

also_consider.name: Anemia
also_consider.rationale: Compensatory sinus tachycardia and palpitations from reduced oxygen-carrying capacity; check CBC and ferritin

also_consider.name: Pregnancy-Related Palpitations
also_consider.rationale: Physiological increase in heart rate and cardiac output; increased ectopy and SVT risk during pregnancy

also_consider.name: Hypoglycemia
also_consider.rationale: Adrenergic symptoms including palpitations, tremor, and diaphoresis; check blood glucose especially in diabetic patients

also_consider.name: Pacemaker Malfunction / Pacemaker-Mediated Tachycardia
also_consider.rationale: Palpitations in patients with implanted devices; interrogate pacemaker/ICD for arrhythmia logs

also_consider.name: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC)
also_consider.rationale: Ventricular arrhythmias originating from RV in young patients; epsilon waves on ECG, family history of sudden death

also_consider.name: Electrolyte Disturbances (Hypokalemia, Hypomagnesemia)
also_consider.rationale: Can trigger arrhythmias including AF, VT, and torsades; check basic metabolic panel and magnesium level

also_consider.name: Catecholaminergic Polymorphic VT (CPVT)
also_consider.rationale: Exercise or emotion-triggered bidirectional VT in structurally normal heart; resting ECG often normal

clinical_reasoning_prompt: This is an evidence-based reference set, not an exhaustive differential. Palpitations are a common symptom with a broad differential ranging from benign to life-threatening. The diagnostic priority is to identify or exclude cardiac arrhythmias, particularly in patients with structural heart disease, syncope, or family history of sudden cardiac death. Always obtain a 12-lead ECG and aim to capture rhythm during symptoms. Consider medication review, substance use history, and systemic causes (thyroid, anemia). A normal resting ECG does not exclude paroxysmal arrhythmias — ambulatory monitoring may be required.
